import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

# Load data from input directory
train = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

# Check if there are any missing values
print(f"Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test.shape}")
print(f"Missing values in train: {train.isnull().sum().sum()}")
print(f"Missing values in test: {test.isnull().sum().sum()}")

# Define feature columns (exclude Id and Cover_Type)
feature_cols = [col for col in train.columns if col not in ["Id", "Cover_Type"]]
print(f"Number of features: {len(feature_cols)}")

# Prepare training data
X_train = train[feature_cols]
y_train = train["Cover_Type"]

# Prepare test data
X_test = test[feature_cols]
test_ids = test["Id"]

# Create a validation split - this data will never be used for training
X_tr, X_val, y_tr, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

print(f"Training split: {X_tr.shape[0]} samples")
print(f"Validation split: {X_val.shape[0]} samples")

# Get the unique classes to ensure we know the expected classes
classes = sorted(y_train.unique())
print(f"Classes: {classes}")

# Train the model on training data only (never on validation)
# Increased n_estimators from 100 to 200 for higher capacity
# Using force_row_wise to optimize performance for large datasets
model = lgb.LGBMClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=15,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=-1,
    force_row_wise=True,
)
model.fit(X_tr, y_tr)

# Evaluate on held-out validation set
y_val_pred = model.predict(X_val)
val_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_val_pred)
print(f"Validation Accuracy: {val_accuracy:.6f}")

# Make predictions on the test set (this is what gets submitted)
y_test_pred = model.predict(X_test)

# Create submission file with exact format
submission = pd.DataFrame({"Id": test_ids, "Cover_Type": y_test_pred})

# Save submission to the correct location
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv with {len(submission)} rows")
